## [GAP ANALYSIS] The new `= ANY(${array})` authorization SQL is never executed against the database

**Severity:** MEDIUM. The riskiest part of the conversion is the array parameter binding in the org and team auth clauses, and that SQL only gets string comparison, never a real query.

### The Problem

The org and team scope tests (around L292-343) do this:

```ts
expect(conditions).toEqual(Prisma.sql`(("teamId" = ANY(${[...]})) AND ...`);
```

That comparison only checks that the service builds the same `strings`/`values` arrays that the test writes by hand. It says nothing about whether Postgres accepts the query or returns the right rows. The single `$queryRaw` test (L480-491) uses `scope: "user"`, which goes through `"userId" = ${id} AND "teamId" IS NULL` and never reaches an `ANY(...)` clause.

### Theory / Proof

With `$queryRaw`, Prisma sends a JS array as a single bound parameter, and Postgres has to infer its element type for `int = ANY($n)`. A type mismatch or a column-name typo would throw at runtime, and a precedence mistake would change which rows come back. Structural `toEqual` can't catch any of these, because the test repeats the same SQL text as the implementation.

### What happens today vs. what will break

The PR description itself says: "I encountered test runner configuration issues, so please verify the tests actually pass." For the org and team paths, a passing suite would still not prove the SQL works.

### Research

The previous `findMany` test ran Prisma's object API, which is type-checked against the view schema. After switching to raw SQL, the only equivalent safety net is running the query.

### Recommendation

Add `$queryRaw` tests for org and team scope that seed one team booking (`isTeamBooking = true`) and one personal booking of a member, and assert both are returned:

```ts
const base = await orgService.getBaseConditions();
const rows = await prisma.$queryRaw<{ id: number }[]>`
  SELECT id FROM "BookingTimeStatusDenormalized" WHERE ${base} ORDER BY id`;
expect(rows.map((r) => r.id)).toEqual([teamBooking.id, personalBooking.id].sort());
```

The team and org tests (L278-346) only compare with toEqual against hand-copied templates. The ANY fragments at insightsBooking.ts:164, 168 and 201 are never executed, and there are no other callers.

## [GAP ANALYSIS] Caching tests were deleted even though the caching code is unchanged

**Severity:** LOW. A regression in the memoization, such as extra DB round-trips or a null filter being rebuilt on every call, would go unnoticed.

### The Problem

The `describe("Caching", ...)` block, which had two tests, was removed rather than migrated. The code it covered is still present:

```ts
async getAuthorizationConditions(): Promise<Prisma.Sql> {
  if (this.cachedAuthConditions === undefined) { ... }
```

### Theory / Proof

`getBaseConditions` calls both getters. Each uncached auth build does 1-3 membership and team queries (`isOrgOwnerOrAdmin`, `findAllByParentId`, `findAllByTeamIds`). The caching is what keeps repeated calls cheap. `cachedFilterConditions` also relies on telling `null` ("no filters") apart from `undefined` ("not computed"), which is easy to break.

### What happens today vs. what will break

The caching still works today. If someone changes the sentinel check to `if (!this.cachedFilterConditions)`, every call rebuilds the conditions and no test fails.

### Research

The PR description says the tests follow the `InsightsRoutingService` test patterns. The old caching tests could have been converted mechanically in the same way as the others.

### Recommendation

Restore the tests using the new SQL format, and assert identity so the test actually proves caching:

```ts
const c1 = await service.getAuthorizationConditions();
const c2 = await service.getAuthorizationConditions();
expect(c2).toBe(c1);
```
kept.evidence: The Caching describe block was removed with no replacement. Memoization is still at insightsBooking.ts:83-95, and the null/undefined sentinel matters because buildFilterConditions returns null at L101/L115. The sibling insightsRouting.integration-test.ts:444-500 still keeps its Caching block. The old toEqual assertions would have passed even without caching, so the suggested toBe identity check is the stronger test.
